scientific_queries.note: Validity check on the programme's own metric: what does ranking by drug marginals actually select?

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round audits the breadth of the metric behind the programme's positive results and finds it far narrower than k.

design.question: when the score is constant within a combination (as drug marginals are), does the top-k contain k distinct discoveries?

reading.good_news: de-duplicating does not lower the hit rate (6.82% versus 6.63%, difference CI includes zero), so the value is not inflated by counting one lucky cell many times
reading.bad_news: the top-20 covers only 2 combinations and 2 drugs, so '20 high-scoring candidates' really means 'the same one or two combinations recommended across many cells'
reading.consequence_for_the_programme: every top-k number reported earlier has an effective number of independent discoveries far below k; and a strategy whose entire output is 'these 1-2 combinations are best' is closer to a single recommendation than to a selection algorithm

limits: the pool is key-level, which is precisely what produces the concentration; a grouped pool would not concentrate this way but marginals degrade there
the de-duplicated rate is a combination-level quantity and is not directly comparable with the key-level rate
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: measure breadth properly with a combination-level top-m curve, m running from 1 to 20

register_updates.C55: new, exploratory: the marginal top-k has very low breadth
